body:
Alex Chen: heads up — during eu-west bringup we saw a repeatable scheduling quirk for low-priority GPUs (preemptible/spot). pods get stuck Pending on nodeAffinity even after node comes back up :thinking_face:
Mira Patel: can you paste the pod describe + node events? wondering if it's the taint/label timing race
Alex Chen: here — snippet from the failing kubelet logs and pod describe:
```
Events:
  Type     Reason             Age   From               Message
  ----     ------             ----  ----               -------
  Warning  FailedScheduling   3m    default-scheduler  0/10 nodes are available: 2 node(s) had taints that the pod didn't tolerate, 8 node(s) didn't match node selector.
```
Logs:
`kubelet: node reacquired but labels not synced before scheduler retry, binding rejected`
```
Mira Patel: ahhh that lines up with the race where kube-controller-manager doesn't reconcile labels fast after node re-registers. we've hit this in canary before
Kai Thompson: on the last repro we temporarily fixed by removing the taint then re-applying. not ideal but good diagnostic. command we ran: `kubectl taint nodes <node> spot=true:NoSchedule- && kubectl taint nodes <node> spot=true:NoSchedule`
Jordan (oncall): what's the impact? production traffic or test fleet?
Alex Chen: test and low-priority batch jobs mostly — but it causes autoscaler to spin up extra nodes because the pods never land so they keep requesting more capacity :grimacing:
Mira Patel: cost + churn pain. propose we add a small retry delay to the scheduler binding window and update bootstrap runbook to include a post-provision label-sync check step
Kai Thompson: agree. also add a quick remediation command to the runbook: `kubectl get nodes -l node.kubernetes.io/instance-type=G5 -o name | xargs -n1 -I {} kubectl annotate {} infra.redwood/label-sync-check=true` then run controller sync job
Alex Chen: I started a draft PR against infra/runbooks: https://git.internal/redwood/infra/runbooks/pull/482 — it includes:
- detection: query for pods Pending with reason FailedScheduling + taint mismatch
- mitigation: taint flip, label resync, and a short autoscaler throttle
- test: manual repro steps and a unit test for node label race
Mira Patel: can we add a note about cloud provider spot termination hooks? some preemptions leave the node cordoned and kubelet in a weird state — add `kubectl uncordon` step explicitly
Jordan (oncall): if we add autoscaler throttle we should metric it. suggest adding an alert `autoscaler.spike-eu-west` so SRE gets paged if this repeats during bootstrapping
sre-bot: Reminder: new alert rule `autoscaler.spike-eu-west` created in alert-manager (pending review)
deploy-bot: PR 482 merged to infra/runbooks (staging). CI: 1 failed, 3 passed.
Alex Chen: nice. CI failed on the new test flake, will fix tomorrow morning. adding a WIP checklist to the thread:
- [x] reproduce failure locally
- [x] draft mitigation steps
- [ ] add doc section to eu-west bootstrap playbook (post-provision label-sync)
- [ ] add alert + dashboard tile for autoscaler spikes
- [ ] runbook playbook merge to master + announce in #eng-infra
Mira Patel: also recording a known-issue entry: "Spot GPU node label-sync race causing Pending pods and autoscaler overshoot" with mitigation steps and cost estimate (we saw ~2.5x expected node churn during a 30m window)
Kai Thompson: gonna add a small automation that checks label age on node join and delays scheduling for up to 30s if labels are stale. will PR to infra/k8s-controllers
Alex Chen: thanks team. I'll update the eu-west bootstrap checklist and ping #eng-infra when PR is green. :wave:
Jordan (oncall): tagging oncall runbook so next shift knows the play: add a quick command block at top of eu-west handoff doc with `kubectl get pods --field-selector=status.phase=Pending -o wide | grep FailedScheduling`
Mira Patel: thumbs up. leaving a short note in the runbook that cost owners should expect a temporary spot churn and budget accordingly for first 2h after region bringup
Alex Chen: last: anyone object to this being marked as a "known issue" in the central provisioning tracker?
Kai Thompson: no objections
Jordan (oncall): approved
Alex Chen: added entry and closed loop. We'll revisit after next eu-west canary run. :thumbsup:
